passages.original: Ἐ. Ἆρα οὖν πάντων μέμνηται ὁ Ἀριστοτέλης;
passages.english: Q. Does Aristotle, then, mention all of them?
passages.notes: Ἐ. and Ἀ. mark the speakers of the dialogue, the questioner (ἐρώτησις) and the answerer (ἀπόκρισις); rendered Q. and A.

passages.original: ’E. Ἀλλὰ ταῦτα μὲν κατὰ Ἀριστοτέλην ὠρίσω, ἐπειδὴ καὶ τούτων μνησθεὶς ὁ αὐτὸς τοὺς ὅρους αὐτῶν τοιούτους πεποίηται· ὅταν λόγου κοινωνῇ τινα τοῦ αὐτοῦ, τοῦ δὲ ὀνόματος μή, ἃ δεῖ καλεῖσθαι πολυώνυμα, τίς ἂν γένοιτο ὅρος;
passages.english: Q. But you have defined these according to Aristotle, since he too, having mentioned them, has framed their definitions in this way. When some things share the same account but not the name, things which should be called polyonyms, what would the definition be?

passages.original: Ὅτι ἡ μὲν ἀνωτάτω καὶ πρώτη γένοιτ᾿ ἂν εἰς δύο, εἰς οὐσίαν καὶ συμβεβηκός· ἀλλ᾿ ἐπεὶ οὐκ ἔστι ταῦτα προενέγκαι ἄνευ τοῦ ἢ καθόλου προενεγκεῖν ἢ ἐπὶ μέρους (αἵ τε γὰρ οὐσίαι ἢ καθολικῶς ἂν προενεχθεῖεν, ὥσπερ τὸ ζῷον, κύων, ἄνθρωπος, ἢ ἐπὶ μέρους, ὥσπερ Σωκράτης, Βουκέφαλος, τά τε συμβεβηκότα καθόλου ἢ ἐπὶ μέρους, ἡ γὰρ ἐπιστήμη καθόλου συμβεβηκός, ἡ δὲ Ἀριστάρχου ἐπιστήμη μερικὸν συμβεβηκός)· ἐπεὶ τοίνυν οὐχ ἁπλῶς οὔτε ἡ οὐσία λέγεται ἀλλ᾿ ἢ καθόλου ἢ μερικῶς καὶ ἀτόμως, οὔτε τὸ συμβεβηκὸς ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῦτο ἢ καθόλου ἢ μερικῶς, εἰς τέσσαρα γίνεται ἡ διαίρεσις, καίτοι πρώτως γενομένη εἰς οὐσίαν καὶ συμβεβηκός.
passages.english: That the highest and first [division] would be into two, into substance and accident. But since it is not possible to put these forward without putting them forward either universally or particularly (for substances would be put forward either universally, such as animal, dog, man, or particularly, such as Socrates, Bucephalus; and accidents [likewise] universally or particularly, for knowledge is a universal accident, while the knowledge of Aristarchus is a particular accident), since, then, neither substance is spoken of simply, but either universally or particularly and individually, nor accident, but this too either universally or particularly, the division comes to be into four, although it was first made into substance and accident.
passages.notes: The opening 'That' (Ὅτι) introduces an answer in the question-and-answer format; the speaker label Ἀ. stands in the preceding context.

passages.original: οὐδὲν γὰρ αὐτοῦ μετέχει, ἄλλ᾿ ἔστι τοῦτο, ὅπερ ἐστίν. οὕτως καὶ τὸ καθόλου ᾗ καθόλου οὐκ ἂν εἴη τοῦ ἀτόμου μέρος, μετέχοι δ᾿ ἂν τὸ ἄτομον πρᾶγμα τοῦ καθόλου, ὡς ἄν ἐν εἴδει ὄντος τοῦ ἀτόμου ἐν τῷ καθόλου ἢ ἐν γένει, ὡς ὁ Σωκράτης ἐν εἴδει μέν ἐστι τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ, ἐν γένει δὲ τῷ ζῴῳ. καὶ τὸ μέρος δὲ ἐν τῷ ὅλῳ, ὡς ἡ χεὶρ ἐν τῷ ὅλῳ σώματι. διὰ τοῦτο οὖν πρόσκειται τὸ ὃ ᾗ τοιοῦτον ἕκαστον, οὐκ ἂν εἴη τὸ ἕτερον.
passages.english: For nothing participates in it, but it is this, just what it is. So too the universal, qua universal, would not be a part of the individual, but the individual thing would participate in the universal, as the individual being in the universal as in a species or in a genus, as Socrates is in the species man and in the genus animal. And the part [is] in the whole, as the hand is in the whole body. For this reason, then, the [phrase] 'that which, as such, each [is], the other would not be' has been added.
passages.notes: The final clause appears to paraphrase a qualifying phrase in Aristotle's definition of 'in a subject'; the Greek is compressed and the exact wording quoted is uncertain.

passages.original: Ἀ. Ὅτι καθ᾿ ὑποκειμένου λέγεται τοῦ τινὸς ἀνθρώπου καὶ οὐκ ἔστι μερικόν τι καὶ ἄτομον, ἀλλὰ κατὰ πλειόνων λέγεται τῷ ἀριθμῷ διαφερόντων. καλῶς οὖν καὶ ὁ Ἀριστοτέλης εἶπεν ὅτι ἄνθρωπος καθ᾿ ὑποκειμένου λέγεται τοῦ τινὸς ἀνθρώπου, ἐν ὑποκειμένῳ δὲ οὐδενί ἐστιν. ὅτι μὲν γὰρ καθόλου ἐστί, καθ᾿ ὑποκειμένου λέγεται τοῦ τινὸς ἀνθρώπου· λέγεται γὰρ ὁ Σωκράτης ἄνθρωπος καὶ ὁ Πλάτων. ἀλλ᾿ οὕτως λέγεται ἄνθρωπος οὐχ ὅτι συμβέβηκε τῷ Σωκράτει ὡς τὸ μουσικὸν καὶ τὸ λευκόν, ἀλλ᾿ ὅτι εἶδός ἐστι τοῦ Σωκράτους ὁ ἄνθρωπος, ὥσπερ καὶ τὸ ζῷον ἐὰν λέγῃς κατὰ τοῦ Σωκράτους, οὐχ ὡς συμβεβηκὸς ἐρεῖς ἀλλ᾿ ὡς γένος· τὰ δὲ εἴδη καὶ τὰ γένη τῶν μὲν οὐσιῶν καὶ αὐτὰ οὐσίαι, τῶν δὲ συμβεβηκότων συμβεβηκότα. αἱ δὲ οὐσίαι οὐκ ἦσαν ἐν ὑποκειμένῳ, ὥστε οὐδὲ τὰ εἴδη οὐδὲ τὰ γένη τῶν οὐσιῶν ἔσται ἐν ὑποκειμένῳ, ἀλλὰ καθ᾿ ὑποκειμένου μὲν ῥηθήσεται τῶν ἀτόμων οὐσιῶν, οὐ μέντοι καὶ ἐν ὑποκειμένῳ ἔσται.
passages.english: A. That it is said of a subject, the particular man, and is not something particular and individual, but is said of many things differing in number. So Aristotle rightly said that man is said of a subject, the particular man, but is in no subject. For because it is universal, it is said of a subject, the particular man: for Socrates is called a man, and so is Plato. But man is said in this way not because it is an accident of Socrates, as musical and white are, but because man is the species of Socrates, just as if you say animal of Socrates, you will say it not as an accident but as a genus. And the species and genera of substances are themselves substances, while those of accidents are accidents. But substances were not in a subject, so that neither the species nor the genera of substances will be in a subject; rather, they will be said of individual substances as of a subject, but they will not also be in a subject.

passages.original: ἐνὸν δὲ καὶ οὕτως, τῶν ὄντων τὰ καθόλου οὐσίαι, τὰ δὲ ἐπὶ μέρους συμβεβηκότα, ἢ ἔμπαλιν τὰ μὲν ἐπὶ μέρους συμβεβηκότα, τὰ δὲ καθόλου οὐσίαι, καὶ τὰ μὲν καθόλου συμβεβηκότα, τὰ δὲ ἐπὶ μέρους οὐσίαι, ἢ ἔμπαλιν τὰ μὲν ἐπὶ μέρους τὰ δὲ καθόλου συμβεβηκότα· ἐνὸν οὖν πολλαχῶς οὕτως διελεῖν, εἰπὲ τοίνυν, ὁ Ἀριστοτέλης κατὰ ποίαν τάξιν τὴν διαίρεσιν
passages.english: And since it is possible [to divide] this way too: of the things that are, the universals are substances and the particulars accidents, or conversely the particulars accidents and the universals substances; and the universals accidents and the particulars substances, or conversely the particulars [...] and the universals accidents. Since, then, it is possible to divide in many ways like this, tell me, then, in what order [did] Aristotle [make] the division?
passages.notes: The passage is repetitive and seems garbled; the second 'conversely' clause repeats the first, and in the final clause a word for the particulars appears to be missing. The sentence breaks off without a main verb, so 'did ... make' is supplied.

passages.original: Ἀ. Μὴ γὰρ ὁ Ἀριστοτέλης ἔφη ἀδύνατον χωρίζεσθαι.
passages.english: A. For Aristotle did not say [it was] impossible to be separated.
passages.notes: Μὴ in a statement is odd; possibly the text should be read as a question ('Did Aristotle not say...?') or is corrupt.

passages.original: Ἀ. Φησὶν ὁ Ἀριστοτέλης τί συμβαίνει· ὅταν ἕτερον καθ᾿ κατηγορῆται ὡς καθ᾿ ὑποκειμένου, ὅσα κατὰ τοῦ λέγεται, πάντα καὶ κατὰ τοῦ ὑποκειμένου ῥηθήσεται.
passages.english: A. Aristotle states what follows: when one thing is predicated of another as of a subject, all the things that are said of what is predicated will also be said of the subject.
passages.notes: The text is defective: read καθ᾿ ἑτέρου for καθ᾿ and κατὰ τοῦ κατηγορουμένου for κατὰ τοῦ (cf. Categories 1b10).

passages.original: ’E. Ἀλλὰ πῶς τοῦτο ἀληθές; ὁ μὲν γὰρ ἄνθρωπος κατὰ Σωκράτους 17v λέγεται καθ᾿ ὑποκειμένου· κατὰ δὲ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου κατηγορεῖται οὐ μόνον ζῷον ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ εἶδος· εἶδος γὰρ ὁ ἄνθρωπος. οὐ μὴν ἔτι Σωκράτους πάντα κατηγορηθήσεται, αλλὰ τὸ μὲν ζῷον κατηγορηθήσεται, οὐκέτι δὲ καὶ τὸ εἶδος·
passages.english: Q. But how is this true? For man is said of Socrates as of a subject; and of man there is predicated not only animal but also species, for man is a species. Yet not all [these] will further be predicated of Socrates: animal will be predicated, but species no longer.
passages.notes: '17v' is a manuscript folio marker, omitted.

passages.original: ’E. Μετὰ 61 ταῦτα περὶ τίνων διδάσκει ὁ Ἀριστοτέλης:
passages.english: Q. After this, about what does Aristotle teach?
passages.notes: '61' is a page or line number from the printed edition and has been left out.

passages.original: Ἀ. Παραδείγματα καὶ τὰ ἴδια, ὡς καὶ Ἀριστοτέλης νῦν μὲν διδοὺς παραδείγματα, ὕστερον δὲ καθ᾿ ἑκάστην κατηγορίαν ζητήσας καὶ δείξας τίνα ἑκάστης ἴδια.
passages.english: A. Examples and the properties, as Aristotle too does, giving examples now, and later, for each category, investigating and showing what the properties of each are.

passages.original: ’E. Τὰς δὲ δευτέρας οὐσίας τίνας εἴρηκεν εἶναι ὁ Ἀριστοτέλης;
passages.english: Q. Which did Aristotle say are the secondary substances?

passages.original: Ἀ. Φησὶν ὁ Ἀριστοτέλης, ὅτι οὔτε ποιότης ἐστὶν μόνον (ἦν γὰρ συμβεβηκός), οὔτε οὐσία μόνον (ἦν γὰρ συγκαταριθμημένη ταῖς οὐσίαις ταῖς δευτέραις), ἀλλὰ τὸ ὅλον τοῦτό ἐστι ποιότης οὐσιώδης· διόπερ οὐκ ἐν τῷ τί ἐστι κατηγορεῖται ἑκάστου οὗ κατηγορεῖται ἀλλ᾿ ἐν τῷ ποῖόν τί ἐστιν.
passages.english: A. Aristotle says that it is neither a quality only (for then it would be an accident) nor a substance only (for it was counted together with the secondary substances), but the whole of it is an essential quality. For this reason it is predicated, of each thing of which it is predicated, not in [answer to] 'what is it?' but in [answer to] 'what sort of thing is it?'
passages.notes: The subject is presumably the differentia, not named in the passage.

passages.original: Ἀ. Οὐδαμῶς· οὐκέτι γὰρ ἐπὶ τῶν δευτέρων οὐσιῶν ἔστιν φάναι τὸ τέδε ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον τὸ τοιόνδε· ὁ γὰρ ἄνθρωπος καὶ τὸ ζῷον οὐκ ἔστιν ἀφωρισμένου τινὸς καὶ ἑνὸς δηλωτικόν· τί γὰρ μᾶλλον τὸν Σωκράτην ἐδήλωσα ἄνθρωπον εἰπὼν ἢ τὸν Πλάτωνα; ὁμοίως δέ, κἂν τὸ ζῷον εἴπω, οὐδὲν μᾶλλον ἀκούεται ὑπὸ τῆς φωνῆς ταύτης ἄνθρωπος ἢ ἵππος ἢ βοῦς ἢ κύων ἤ τι τῶν ἄλλων ζῴων. οὐκ ἐφαρμόζει οὖν ἐπὶ τῶν δευτέρων οὐσιῶν τὸ τόδε ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον τὸ τοιόνδε.
passages.english: A. Not at all; for in the case of secondary substances one can no longer say 'this something', but rather 'such a sort'; for man and animal do not indicate something determinate and one. For why did I indicate Socrates by saying 'man' any more than Plato? Likewise, if I say 'animal', by this word a man is understood no more than a horse or an ox or a dog or any of the other animals. So 'this something' does not fit secondary substances, but rather 'such a sort'.
passages.notes: τέδε is read as τόδε (scanning error).

passages.original: ’E. Ἆρα οὖν ὁ Ἀριστοτέλης τῶν δύο σημαινομένων εμνήσθη;
passages.english: Q. Did Aristotle, then, mention the two meanings?

passages.original: ’A. Ὅρον μὲν αὐτῶν γενικώτατον οὐκ ἔστιν ποιήσασθαι, ὡς οὐδ’ ἐπὶ τῶν ἄλλων, τὴν δὲ ἐπίνοιαν ἔστιν συλλαβόντας ἀποδοῦναι, ὃ πεποίηκεν καὶ Ἀριστοτέλης εἰπὼν πρός τι εἶναι ταῦτα, ὅσα αὐτὰ ἅπερ ἐστὶν ἑτέρων εἶναι λέγεται ἢ ὁπωσοῦν ἄλλως πρὸς ἕτερον.
passages.english: A. It is not possible to give a definition of them, since they are a most general genus, just as [it is not possible] in the case of the others either; but it is possible to grasp and render the notion [of them], which is what Aristotle too has done, saying that those things are relatives which are said to be just what they are of other things, or in some other way whatever in relation to another.
passages.notes: 'Ὅρον μὲν αὐτῶν γενικώτατον' is awkward as printed; taken as 'a definition of them, [being] most general', i.e. of a most general genus.

passages.original: ἔστι δὲ τὸ τοιοῦτον ζήτημα, ὅποῖον ἐζητεῖτο παρὰ τοῖς παλαιοῖς, εἰ ὥσπερ τῶν ἄλλων σχημάτων ἔστι τοσοῦτον χωρίον περιλαβεῖν, ὅσονπερ ὁ κύκος, οὕτως καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ τετραγώνου. καὶ φαίνετα μὲν ὅτι ἔστι τις ἀπόδειξις, καθ' ἣν ἔστι τετράγωνον σχῆμα κύκλῳ περιλαβεῖν ὥσπερ καὶ ἄλλα σχήματα, οὐχ εὕρηται δὲ πῶς, ἢ εἰ καὶ εὕρηται, ὥς φασί τινες, ἀλλ' ἐπὶ Ἀριστοτέλους οὔπω εὕρητο. ὥστε ὄντος ἐπιστητοῦ τοῦ παραλαβεῖν τετράγωνον χωρίον κύκλῳ οὐδέπω ἡ ἐπιστήμη εὕρητο. ἐπεὶ καὶ τὸ τὰ ἐκλείψεις τοῦ ἡλίου καὶ τῆς σελήνης γνῶναι καὶ προειπεῖν ἔστιν o μέν, ὥσπερ καὶ εὕρηται, πρὸ μέντοι θαλοῦ οὐδέπω ἦν ὄντος τοῦ ἐπιστηντοῦ.
passages.english: The problem is of the kind that was investigated among the ancients: whether, just as with the other figures it is possible to enclose an area as great as the circle, so too in the case of the square. And it appears that there is some demonstration according to which it is possible to make a square figure equal to a circle, just as [with] other figures too, but it has not been found how; or, if it has in fact been found, as some say, still in Aristotle's time it had not yet been found. So, although the squaring of a circle by a square area is knowable, the knowledge [of it] had not yet been found. For the knowing and foretelling of the eclipses of the sun and the moon is also [knowable], as indeed it has been found; yet before Thales [the knowledge] did not yet exist, though the knowable existed.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: κύκος for κύκλος, φαίνετα for φαίνεται, ἐπιστηντοῦ for ἐπιστητοῦ, θαλοῦ for Θάλου. 'περιλαβεῖν/παραλαβεῖν' understood as constructing a square equal in area to a circle. The phrase 'ἔστιν o μέν' is garbled; rendered as 'is [knowable]'.

passages.original: Ἐ. Ἀλλ᾿ ἐπεὶ ἔφη ὁ Ἀριστοτέλης τὸ ὡς ἐπὶ τὸ πολὺ προϋπαρ- χόντων πραγμάτων τὰς ἐπιστήμας λαμβάνομεν, ἐπ᾿ ὀλίγων γὰρ ἢ ἐπ᾿ οὐδενὸς ἴδοι τις ἂν ἅμα τῷ ἐπιστητῷ τὴν ἐπιστήμην γινομένην, ἐπὶ τίνων ἅμα ἡ ἐπιστήμη συνυφίσταται;
passages.english: Q. But since Aristotle said that for the most part we acquire knowledge of things that already exist beforehand, for in few cases or in none would one see knowledge coming into being at the same time as the knowable, in which cases does knowledge come into existence together with [its object]?

passages.original: ’E. Ἀλλ᾿ ἐπεὶ ἄτοπον τῶν πρός τί τινας παραδέξασθαι τῶν οὐσιῶν, τί πεποίηκεν ὁ Ἀριστοτέλης;
passages.english: Q. But since it is absurd to admit some substances among the relatives, what has Aristotle done?

passages.original: ’E. Ἀριστοτέλης δὲ τί ἔφη περὶ τῆς τοιαύτης ὑπογραφῆς τῶν προς τι;
passages.english: Q. And what did Aristotle say about such a description of relatives?

passages.original: Ἐ. Σφοδρῶς μὲν οὐκ ἀξιοῖ ὁ Ἀριστοτέλης μὴ πολλάκις ἐπεσκεμμένους, τὸ μέντοι ἠπορηκέναι ἐφ᾿ ἑκάστου αὐτῶν οὐκ ἄχρηστον εἶναι. δυνατὸ γάρ τινα εἰπεῖν κἀπὶ τῶν μερῶν ὅτι ὡρισμένως εἴσεται· ὁ γὰρ ἰδὼν τίς ἡ χείρ ἐστιν, ὅτι καὶ τοῦδέ ἐστιν εἴσεται ὡρισμένως· ὁ γὰρ δὴ τοῦ ἐγκεκαλυμμένου ὁρῶν χεῖρα γινώσκει μὲν χεῖρα, * * τὸν γάρ τινά ἐστιν εἰ- δέναι τὸ τήνδε γινώσκειν εἰ ἔστιν τοῦδε.
passages.english: Q. Aristotle does not think it right to make firm pronouncements without having examined [the matter] many times; yet [he holds] that to have raised difficulties about each of them is not useless. For one could say in the case of parts too that one will know [the correlate] definitely; for whoever has seen what the hand is will also know definitely that it is the hand of this [person]. For indeed someone who sees the hand of a man who is veiled recognizes a hand, but [...] for it is [not possible] for him to know, in recognizing this, whose it is.
passages.notes: The edition marks a lacuna (* *); the closing words are corrupt (τὸν γάρ τινα...) and the sense 'it is not possible to know whose it is' is conjectural. The speaker siglum Ἐ. (question) seems inappropriate for an answer.

passages.original: Ἐ. Ἀλλ᾿ εἰ τὰ ὁμωνύμως λεγόμενά φησιν αὐτὸς πλεοναχῶς λέγεσθαι, πῶς πλεοναχῶς λέγεσθαι τὴν ποιότητά φησιν ὁ Ἀριστοτέλης;
passages.english: Q. But if he himself says that things called homonymously are said in many ways, how does Aristotle say that quality is said in many ways?

passages.original: Ἀ. Ὡς μὲν εἴδη ἀλλήλων οὐ διενήνοχεν ὥσπερ ὁ ἄνθρωπος τοῦ βοός· οὐ γὰρ διαφέρει ἀλλήλων εἰδοποιοῖς διαφοραῖς ὥσπερ ὁ ἵππος τοῦ ἀνθρώπου. ἀριθμῷ δὲ ἀλλήλων διενήνοχεν ὥσπερ Σωκράτης Πλάτωνος· εἰδοποιοῖς μὲν γὰρ διαφοραῖς οὐ διενήνοχεν Σωκράτης Πλάτωνος, ἰδιότητι δὲ συνδρομῆς ποιοτήτων, καθ᾿ ἣν εἰδοποιῷ διενήνοχεν Πλάτων Σωκράτους. ὥσπερ οὖν τὸ λευκὸν τὸ πολυχρονιώτερον τοῦ ἐφημέρου λευκοῦ τῷ εἴδει μὲν οὐ διαφέρει (καθὸ γὰρ λευκόν ἐστι, οὐ διαφέρει)·
passages.english: A. They do not differ from one another as species, as man [differs] from ox; for they do not differ from one another by specific differences, as horse [differs] from man. But they differ from one another in number, as Socrates [differs] from Plato; for Socrates does not differ from Plato by specific differences, but by the peculiarity of a concurrence of qualities, according to which Plato differs from Socrates in a [non-]specific way. Just as, then, the longer-lasting white does not differ in species from the white that lasts a day (for insofar as it is white, it does not differ);
passages.notes: καθ᾿ ἣν εἰδοποιῷ διενήνοχεν seems corrupt: 'by a specific [difference]' contradicts the preceding clause; perhaps a negative or a different word has dropped out. Translated tentatively.

passages.original: Ἐ. Πῶς οὖν τοῦτο εἴρηκεν ὁ Ἀριστοτέλης;
passages.english: Q. How then has Aristotle said this?

passages.original: Ὅτι ἐκεῖ μὲν κατὰ τὸ διακεῖσθαί πως τὸ θερμὸν καὶ τὸ ψυχρόν, εἰ καὶ μὴ ἐπιμόνως, διαθέσεις ἔλεγεν, ἐνταῦθα δὲ κατὰ τὸ πάθος ἐμποιεῖν εἰς ἄλλο, τὸ δὲ αὐτὸ κατ’ ἄλλο καὶ ἄλλο λαμβανόμενον δύναται ἄλλου καὶ ἄλλου εἶναι εἴδους, ὡς † ὁ πατὴρ καθὸ μὲν Σωκράτης, οὐσία ἂν εἴη, καθὸ δὲ πατήρ, τῶν πρός τι. οὕτω γὰρ καὶ ἡ θερμότης καθὸ μὲν διατίθησί πως τὸ ὑποκείμενον, διάθεσις ἂν εἴη, κἂν ἔμμονος γένοιτο καὶ δυσανάλυτος, ἕξις ἂν γένοιτο, καθὸ δὲ τὴν αἴσθησιν θερμαίνει τῶν πελαζόντων, παθητικὴ ἂν εἴη ποιότης.
passages.english: That there he called hot and cold dispositions according to [a thing's] being disposed in some way, even if not lastingly, but here [he calls them qualities] according to producing an affection in something else; and the same thing, taken in respect of one thing and another, can belong to one category and another, as † the father, insofar as he is Socrates, would be a substance, but insofar as he is a father, [belongs] among relatives. So too heat, insofar as it disposes the subject in some way, would be a disposition, and if it became lasting and hard to dissolve, it would become a state; but insofar as it heats the perception of those who come near, it would be an affective quality.
passages.notes: The edition marks corruption (†) before 'the father'; perhaps 'Sophroniscus' or similar originally stood here. 'Form/kind' (εἴδους) rendered as 'category' by sense.

passages.original: ᾿Α. Ἡμορφὴ διχῶς λέγεται παρὰ τῷ ᾿Αριστοτέλει· καθ᾿ ἓν μὲν γὰρ σημαινόμενον τὰς οὐσιώδεις μορφὰς λέγει, καθ᾿ ἕτερον δὲ τὰ ἐπὶ τοῖς οὐσιώδεσιν εἴδεσιν ἐπιφαινόμενα καὶ κατὰ τὰς ἐπιφανείας τυπώματα, καθ᾿ ἃ καλά τε λεγομεν καὶ εὔμορφα τὰ εἴδη οὐδὲν ἐφαπτόμενοι τῶν οὐσιωδῶν.
passages.english: A. Shape (morphē) is spoken of in two ways by Aristotle: in one meaning he speaks of the essential forms, in the other of the impressions that appear upon the essential forms and on the surfaces, in respect of which we call forms beautiful and shapely without touching at all on what is essential.

passages.original: Ἀ. Ὅτι καὶ ὁ Ἀριστοτέλης ἔφη· ἴσως οὖν καὶ ἄλλος τρόπος φανείη ἂν ποιότητος.
passages.english: A. Because Aristotle also said: 'Perhaps, then, some other kind of quality might also appear.'

passages.original: ὑπελάμβανον μὴ ἐπιδέχεσθαι τὸ μᾶλλον καὶ τὸ ἧττον ὡς τὰς ἀρετὰς <τὰς ἀρετὰς καὶ> κατὰ ταύτας <ποιούς, τινὰς> τινὰς δὲ καὶ ποιοὺς ἐπιδέχεσθαι ἐπίτασιν καὶ ἄνεσιν, ὡς πάσας <τὰς> μέσας<> καὶ τὰς μέσας ποιότητας καὶ τοὺς κατὰ ταύτας ποιούς. ἧς γεγόνασι δόξης οἱ ἀπὸ τῆς Στοᾶς. τρίτη γέγονεν, ἧς καὶ ὁ Ἀριστοτέλης μέμνηται, ἣ τὰς μὲν ἕξεις ἀνεπιτάτους καὶ ἀνανέτους ὑπελάμβανεν εἶναι, τοὺς δὲ κατ’ αὐτὰς ποιοὺς ἐπιδέχεσθαι τὸ μᾶλλον καὶ τὸ ἧττον, οὐ πάντας μέντοι.
passages.english: [...] supposed that [some] do not admit the more and the less, such as the virtues and those [who are] qualified according to them, but that some [states], and some qualified [things], do admit intensification and relaxation, such as all the intermediate qualities and those qualified according to them. Of this opinion were the Stoics. A third [school] arose, which Aristotle also mentions, which supposed that the states are incapable of intensification and relaxation, but that those qualified according to them admit the more and the less, though not all of them.
passages.notes: The opening is fragmentary: the preceding sentence breaks off in a lacuna, and the text here contains duplicated words and editorial supplements in angle brackets (e.g. 'τὰς ἀρετὰς <τὰς ἀρετὰς καὶ>', '<ποιούς, τινὰς> τινὰς', '<τὰς> μέσας<> καὶ τὰς μέσας'), apparently conflating transmitted text and conjectural restoration. The translation follows the evident sense, rendering each phrase once. 'Qualified' renders ποιοί, the things or persons characterised by a quality.

passages.original: ’E. Τοσαῦτα μὲν περὶ τοῦ ποιεῖν καὶ τοῦ πάσχειν εἴρηται ὑπὸ Αριστοτέλους. περὶ δὲ τοῦ κεῖσθαι τί ἄν εἴποις; ’A. Ὅτι ἡ μὲv θέσις τῶν πρός τι δέδεικται ἤδη, τὸ δὲ κεῖσθαι οὐκ ἔτι, ἀλλὰ παρώνυμον· ἄλλης γὰρ κατηγορίας, τῆς τοῦ κεῖσθαι.
passages.english: Q. So much has been said by Aristotle about acting and being acted upon. But what would you say about being-in-a-position? A. That position (thesis) has already been shown to belong among relatives, whereas being-in-a-position (keisthai) no longer does, but is paronymous; for it belongs to another category, that of being-in-a-position.
passages.notes: The speaker marks ’E. and ’A. presumably stand for ἐρώτησις/ἀπόκρισις (question/answer).

passages.original: ’E. Ὑπολείπονται δὲ κατηγορίαι ἔτι τρεῖς· ἥ τε τοῦ ποτὲ καὶ ἡ τοῦ ποῦ καὶ ή τοῦ ἔχειν. καὶ ὅτι μὲv ὁ Ἀριστοτέλης οὐδὲν περὶ αὐτῶν εἴρηκεν, δῆλον· σὺ δὲ τἱ ἄν εἴποις περὶ τούτων;
passages.english: Q. Three categories still remain: that of when, that of where, and that of having. That Aristotle has said nothing about them is clear; but what would you say about them?
